text:
incident-bot: PAGER: High p99 tail latency observed for streaming endpoints (/v1/stream) across eu-west-2 starting ~1864527850. Automated SLO monitor: p99 > 2.5s, error budget burn > 35%. Paging oncall: @dylan and @neteng-bot.

Dylan: ack, I'm on it. grabbing graphs and will triage.

priya: grabbing traces now — seeing spikes in TLS handshake times and a rise in retransmits between AZ-b and AZ-c nodes. p95 elevated too but p99 jumps are the problem. dashboard -> https://redwood.app/dashboards/streams/slo?range=15m :eyes:

miguel: I see a big increase in NAT ephemeral port reuse failures in eu-west-2-a/b. Could be SNAT exhaustion on nat-gw-a causing TCP conn resets and extra RTTs while clients retry. Starting tcpdump on proxy-1 in AZ-b.

sam: any customer reports? CS monitoring flagged 3 enterprise customers with streaming stalls about 3m ago. cc @customer-success

customer-success: we have 3 customers reporting intermittent stalls and reconnects (no data loss reported). Drafting a short status note: "We're investigating streaming interruptions in eu-west-2, possible egress network congestion; we'll follow up within 30m."

priya: query I'm running: 
```
max_over_time(histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(stream_request_duration_bucket[5m]))[15m:1m])
```
Result: p99 peaked at 3.2s at 1864527868 and stayed >2s until 1864528000.

miguel: tcpdump snippet (trimmed):
```
15:44:20.123456 IP svc-proxy > client: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
15:44:23.987654 IP svc-proxy > client: [TCP Retransmission] Flags [S], seq 0, ...
15:44:24.000123 IP client > svc-proxy: Flags [RST], seq 1, ...
```
Shows handshake retransmit then RST from client. Lots of SYN retransmits seen across multiple sockets.

dylan: ok. hypothesis: NAT gateway A is running out of ephemeral ports causing connection resets and forcing clients to reconnect (higher handshake latency). Two mitigations: 1) shift egress for streaming nodes in AZ-b to nat-gw-b (alternate gateway) and 2) apply temporary connection keepalive tuning to reduce churn. I'll run failover to nat-gw-b as immediate mitigation.

neteng-bot: Suggested mitigation runbook referenced: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/nat-ephemeral-exhaustion. Next step: replace route table association for subnet-sub-b to nat-gw-b, then monitor SYN/retransmit counts.

priya: command to rotate egress (run in ops shell):
```
# AWS CLI (ops role)
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0abc123 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-0def456
```
(ensure dry-run=false, rolling change per subnet)

miguel: executed rotate on two subnets in AZ-b at 1864527955. Confirming tcpdump now shows reduced retransmits. Monitoring metrics...

priya: metrics update: p99 dropped from 3.2s -> 1.1s within 90s of the switch. p95 back near baseline. error budget burn trending down.

dylan: nice. leaving a temporary rule in place and creating a short-lived alert suppression for this signal so we don't wake everyone while we observe. will start postmortem doc and handoff to priya for follow-up.

customer-success: updated customers with note: "We've completed an initial mitigation; connectivity is improving. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline."

sam: any config changes we need to make permanent? e.g., increase NAT capacity or move to NAT with auto-scaling?

miguel: follow-ups: 1) provision additional NAT gateways in eu-west-2 and enable HA route priority, 2) increase ephemeral port range on proxies where possible, 3) add synthetic streaming checks that exercise long-lived TLS sessions. I'll open infra tickets.

dylan: handoff: I'm unpaginating at 1864528100, leaving ownership with priya for the postmortem and persist tasks. Priya — you're the incident lead now.

priya: taking it. created incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1864527890. Assigning follow-up tasks and ETA for RCA in 48h.

incident-bot: NOTE: incident severity set to Sev3, postmortem template created and assigned to priya. Follow-up reminders scheduled. :white_check_mark:

dylan: thanks all — great cross-team run.

priya: final status 1864528205: streaming p99 stable ~1.0s, no new customer complaints. closing active paging, will publish RCA draft tomorrow.
